title: Reunion
text: Your 20-year school reunion is this weekend.

outcomes.text: Everyone asked what I do now. I enjoyed answering.
My old crush is doing way better than me.
I reconnected with an old friend, {old.first}.
Most of the class had changed so much I barely recognised them. I spent the evening at the bar, talking to the one person who hadn't.
Someone asked what I'd done with my life and I gave the wrong answer. I drove home in silence.
Some chapters stay closed.
A friend sent me photos, and I was weirdly jealous. There was a story I'll never know.
I spent the weekend in a cabin, which I consider a better use of twenty years.

title: House fire
text: Your neighbor's house is on fire, and you hear a dog barking inside.

outcomes.text: I got the dog out! The whole street cheered.
The smoke was too much. Firefighters pulled us both out.
The firefighters saved the dog.
The dog was saved, but the fire spread to two houses. The neighbours thanked me for the call.
The fire station was four minutes away. The house was lost, the dog and family weren't. I sat on the kerb afterwards.
I called and then ran in. I shouldn't have. A fireman dragged me out and scolded me gently.

choices.label: Shout for the neighbours and get the hose

outcomes.text: Four of us made a bucket chain. The fire brigade found it half out. We were thanked and wet.
The hose was too short and the fire too big. I helped from the street.

title: Lost kid
text: A little kid is crying alone in the mall.

outcomes.text: Their mom hugged me like I was family.
It took forty minutes and a sticker, but we found them. The mother insisted on giving me her number.
The kid wouldn't let go of my hand, and a security guard looked at me with suspicion. I was mortified.
Security took over.
Security lost track of the child for an agonising five minutes. I watched from a distance.
The kid was returned to their parents in under ten minutes. I felt like part of a system that works.

choices.label: Stay with them until someone arrives

outcomes.text: I held a small, sticky hand for twenty minutes. The parent arrived in a panic and the child, who'd been calm, burst into tears.
Nobody arrived for an hour. I became the child's favourite person and felt oddly responsible.
Best 60 seconds of my life.
The parachute opened late. I landed in a cow field.
Next year, for sure.
I meant it. The year passed and I had found a new reason to put it off.
I booked it then and there, and it was the best fall of my life.

choices.label: Book it for a specific date with a friend

outcomes.text: We jumped on a Saturday in June. It was the most terrifying thing I've done.
We booked it and the weather turned. We rebooked. And rebooked.

title: DNA test
text: You took a mail-in DNA test for fun. The results are in.

outcomes.text: The DNA test says I'm 3% Viking. I bought a helmet.
The DNA test says I'm related to half of a small town in the mountains.

title: Old rival
text: You run into {rv.first}, your old rival, at a coffee shop.

outcomes.text: We laughed about the old days. We're friends now.
They were cold and I was left holding an olive branch. We parted awkwardly.
We talked for two hours, then exchanged numbers. A year later they were at my wedding.
I hid behind a menu.
They saw me. They pretended too. We never spoke of it.
They came straight over anyway, and I had to rise to the occasion. It went better than I deserved.
They gloated back. It became a competition.
My gloating backfired when they turned out to be doing much better than I'd assumed.
They were dazzled, and I went home feeling hollow.

title: Retirement party
text: {par.first} is retiring and throwing a party.

outcomes.text: {par.first} cried. So did I.
I'd written it on a napkin and lost the napkin. I improvised and it was better.
I choked up halfway through. {par.first} stood and finished it with me.
The room roared. {par.first} laughed hardest.
A joke about {par.first}'s cooking landed badly. A relative left.
I told a story from my childhood that nobody knew. {par.first} wept laughing.
{par.first} noticed I wasn't there.
I sent a card. It arrived three weeks late. {par.first} put it on the mantel anyway.
Work ran over. {par.first} said "I understand", in a way that I didn't.

title: Loan request
text: {kid.first} asks to borrow $10,000 to start a business.

outcomes.text: {kid.first}'s business took off! {kid.He} paid me back double.
The business failed. {kid.first} is embarrassed.
{kid.first} rolled {kid.his} eyes, then took the advice.
{kid.first} didn't take it, made every mistake I'd warned about, and did well anyway. I am both proud and annoyed.
The advice saved {kid.first} from signing a bad lease. They called to thank me and I pretended I hadn't been worried.
{kid.first} was disappointed.
{kid.first} found the money elsewhere and the business took off. I wasn't in the story.
The business folded in six months. I was quietly relieved and guilty about it.

title: Grandparent
text: {kid.first} just had a baby. You're a grandparent!

outcomes.text: {kid.first} just had a baby. I'm a grandparent!

title: Checkup
text: Your doctor wants to run more tests after your checkup.

outcomes.text: All clear. Just a scare.
They caught something early. Treatment worked.
I skipped the tests. Hopefully that was fine.
It was nothing. I felt foolish for having worried and irresponsible for having skipped.
It wasn't nothing. By the time I went back, the options were narrower.

choices.label: Ask about the risks of each test first

outcomes.text: The doctor was candid. I did the two that mattered and skipped the rest.
The doctor was candid, and the candour frightened me more than the tests would have.
I picked up pottery. My first bowl looks like a hat.
I got really into birdwatching. I have binoculars now.
I started running. My knees filed a complaint.
I learned to bake bread. Everyone at work loves me now.
Someone anonymously paid for my groceries. I paid it forward the next day.

title: Moving day
text: {fr.first} begs you to help move a piano up four flights of stairs.

outcomes.text: We got the piano up. My back will never forgive me.
Halfway up the third flight, the piano got stuck. We were there for three hours and one of us wept.
The piano turned out to be out of tune. We moved it anyway, then drank a beer on its lid.
{fr.first} knew I was lying.
The dentist's receptionist called to ask about my missed appointment. I hadn't made one. {fr.first} heard.
{fr.first} hired movers instead. We both pretended nothing happened, and did it well.

choices.label: Offer to help with boxes, not the piano

outcomes.text: Boxes I could do. The piano was moved by professionals. {fr.first} was relieved I'd turned up at all.
The professionals dropped the piano on the stairs. I'm told it's still out of tune.
A new pandemic swept the world. Everything shut down for months.
A major war broke out overseas. The news was hard to watch.
Scientists announced a cure for a common disease. The world celebrated.
Humans landed on Mars. I watched it live with tears in my eyes.
A stranger named {sib.first} messaged me: a DNA site says we're half-siblings.
